action: In general, a standard system update will make all the necessary changes.
description:
It was discovered that PHP did not properly validate the size of MySQL
server packets in the mysqlnd driver. A malicious server could possibly use
this issue to cause PHP to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This
issue was only addressed in Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu
24.04 LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, and Ubuntu 26.10. (CVE-2025-1218)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly handled response buffer sizes in the
SOAP HTTP client. A malicious server could possibly use this issue to cause
PHP to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or execute arbitrary code.
(CVE-2025-14181)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly handled certain TAR archive headers
in the Phar extension. An attacker could possibly use this issue to inject
arbitrary files into a crafted archive. (CVE-2026-6103)

It was discovered that PHP did not limit recursion depth when parsing
certain SOAP requests. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to
cause PHP to crash, resulting in a denial of service. (CVE-2026-91765)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly handled authentication headers when
following HTTP redirects. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue
to obtain sensitive information. (CVE-2026-91766)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly handled wildcard names in TLS server
certificates. A malicious server could possibly use this issue to cause PHP
to crash, resulting in a denial of service. This issue did not affect
Ubuntu 14.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-91767)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly validated IPv6 client addresses in
the FastCGI client access check. A remote attacker could possibly use this
issue to bypass access restrictions. This issue did not affect Ubuntu 14.04
LTS. (CVE-2026-91768)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly performed TLS peer name
verification. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to
impersonate a trusted server. (CVE-2026-91769)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly handled certain stream filter
options. An attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive
information. (CVE-2026-92842)

It was discovered that PHP incorrectly handled empty Location headers when
following HTTP redirects. A malicious server could possibly use this issue
to redirect the client to an unintended location. This issue did not affect
Ubuntu 14.04 LTS. (CVE-2026-93682)
isummary: Several security issues were fixed in PHP.
summary: php8.5, php8.3, php8.1, php7.4, php7.2, php7.0, php5 vulnerabilities
